subject: NovaMed on‑prem landing charter: node pools, PV strategy, and air‑gapped constraints
messages:
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@novamed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Planning: on‑prem cluster constraints and acceptance criteria

Hi Grace / Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Attached is a condensed requirements PDF from our infra team (attached: novamed_onprem_requirements_v1.pdf) — high level items:

- Air‑gapped site (no outbound internet except scheduled approved egress).
- Two racks, each with 6 GPU hosts (A100 equivalent), separate top‑of‑rack switches.
- Need multi‑AZ‑like failure domains within the site for availability.
- PV requirements: encrypted blockstore, hot cache NVMe for model KV cache, and an archival NFS/backup target.
- KMS integration for keys (single HSM managed by us) and strict audit logs.

We'd like a short landing charter: recommended nodepool breakdown, PV class mapping, network gating for control plane, and a minimal acceptance test plan for tenant onboarding. Can Redwood draft that and include any red flags for networking or PCI/SOC constraints?

Proposed time to sync: tomorrow 10:30am PT. If that doesn't work, please propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Rajiv
Ops Lead, NovaMed

---
Attachment: novamed_onprem_requirements_v1.pdf (PDF, 320KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@novamed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-25T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Planning: on‑prem cluster constraints and acceptance criteria

Rajiv — thanks for the doc, this is helpful. We've sketched an initial landing charter below (short form) and attached a mutual action plan spreadsheet that maps owners and dates. High‑level notes:

- Nodepool proposal:
  * control-plane (3 VMs, non‑GPU): dedicated to kube‑api and control plane services. Must be placed in a separate mgmt VLAN with ACLs to customer KMS.
  * inference-gpu-hot (6 hosts across racks): GPU instances for production inference with local NVMe for model KV cache; use StatefulSet PVs for sticky caching.
  * inference-gpu-cold (6 hosts reserved for lower‑priority/overflow): burst/spot pool controlled by autoscaler with preemption allowed.
  * system-workloads (3 hosts): monitoring, logging, sidecar services; encrypted blockstore for retention.

- Storage mapping:
  * KV cache: local NVMe, ephemeral but with hot‑checkpointing to a PV class backed by encrypted block storage every 15m.
  * Model artifacts: encrypted blockstore (fast), replicated across racks using synchronous replication at block layer where possible.
  * Backups/archives: NFS target mounted read‑only for clusters; retention policy 90d by default.

- Network & control plane:
  * Control plane sits in a management VLAN with egress strictly through a jump host (approved egress window).
  * BGP peering is OK if you provide route targets; else we can use static routes per rack.
  * CNI recommendation: Calico in policy only mode (no IPAM) — you will manage IPAM on your DHCP/infra.

- Acceptance tests (minimal):
  * Control plane HA failover and API latency under 500ms for 95th percentile.
  * Successful KV cache warm‑up on a canary model in 60s.
  * Encrypted PV attach/detach and read/write checks at expected throughput.
  * End‑to‑end inference SLO test (p95 < 120ms for small prompts).

Next steps: Karthik and Jordan will convert this into a one‑page landing charter and an action tracker. We can review on the sync. Does 10:30am PT still work?

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@novamed.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-25T14:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Planning: on‑prem cluster constraints and acceptance criteria

Adding a couple of implementation constraints and a suggestion for node sizing:

- Kubernetes version: we recommend 1.30.x LTS (kernel ABI tested with our runtime).
- Control plane VMs: 4 vCPU / 32GB RAM, dedicated SSDs for etcd. etcd should run on two nodes with a read‑only follower on the third to reduce write latency.
- GPU hosts: 8‑core CPU, 256GB RAM, NVMe for cache (1TB), 2 x 10Gbps NICs (bonded). Reserve 30% of NVMe for OS and container overlay to avoid eviction storms.
- Node selectors / taints: inference pools must be tainted to prevent system pods from landing. System workloads should use tolerations.
- PV classes: two classes with encryption at rest: fast-block (io2‑equivalent) and nvme-ephemeral (local). We'll manage CSI drivers; you will need a sidecar for safe node drain of GPU workloads.

Network gating note: because this is effectively air‑gapped, we propose a scheduled egress window (30m each night) where control plane can pull images from a preapproved registry mirror. Alternatively, provide an internal mirror/proxy; that will simplify upgrades.

I'll put these into the one‑pager before the call. If anyone has constraints around HSM connectivity (we need to reach the HSM from control plane), flag that now — otherwise we'll assume a routed mgmt path exists.

— Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Rajiv Sharma <rajiv@novamed.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-04-26T15:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Planning: on‑prem cluster constraints and acceptance criteria

Thanks — 10:30 worked well. Quick follow ups from our side after the sync:

1) HSM: we'll open a routed mgmt path from the management VLAN to the HSM appliance on a dedicated L3 hop.
2) Registry mirror: our infra team will stand up a local registry mirror and provide credentials before the first deploy.
3) Can you add a short procedure in the charter for draining GPU nodes safely (we need the exact CSI call sequence)?

If you can push the one‑page charter and the action tracker by end of day tomorrow, we'll route it for internal security approval. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Rajiv
Ops Lead, NovaMed
